visualDescription.sceneDescriptionEn: A black and white line engraving depicting a group of men in a wooded setting. In the foreground, a man with long hair, wearing a loincloth and leggings, stands and touches the face of a seated man who is dressed in European-style clothing, including a collared shirt and trousers. Behind them, three other men stand in the background, appearing to observe the interaction. The style is characteristic of 19th-century book illustrations.

visualDescription.recognizableCharactersOrPeopleEn: Five male figures: one seated man in European-style attire and four men in indigenous-style attire, including one standing in the foreground and three standing in the background.
visualDescription.uncertaintyNotes: The specific cultural or historical identity of the figures is not explicitly stated in the image, though the attire suggests a depiction of indigenous people and a European settler or explorer. suggestedMatch.modelRationaleNotVerified: The illustration depicts a group of men in a wooded setting with a seated European-style figure and indigenous figures interacting. Chapter 29, paragraph 57 describes the moment where warriors (indigenous) approach Heyward (European-style clothing) to bind him, which aligns with the visual of a group of men surrounding a seated figure in a forest setting.
suggestedMatch.suggestedAltArNotApproved: A 19th-century engraving showing a seated man in European clothing being approached by indigenous warriors in a forest, reflecting the scene where Heyward is taken into custody by the Delawares.
